holidays.name: Garden Meditation Day
holidays.description: A day to step outside, sit among the plants, and quietly soak in the sights, smells, and sounds of a garden. Weeds, worms, and buzzing bees all count as part of the zen experience.
holidays.origin: Garden Meditation Day is an unofficial observance that grew out of the wellness and mindfulness movements, encouraging people to combine gardening with meditation each spring.
holidays.funFact: Studies have found that just 30 minutes of gardening can lower cortisol levels more effectively than reading indoors.

holidays.name: World Press Freedom Day
holidays.description: A serious but important observance celebrating the fundamental principles of press freedom and honoring journalists who risk their lives to report the truth.
holidays.origin: Proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1993 following a recommendation from UNESCO, inspired by the 1991 Windhoek Declaration of African journalists.
holidays.funFact: The Windhoek Declaration was written in Namibia, and the UNESCO/Guillermo Cano World Press Freedom Prize is awarded each year on this date.

holidays.name: Textiles Day
holidays.description: A celebration of all things fabric, from cozy quilts to fancy silks, honoring the art and craft of weaving, knitting, and sewing.
holidays.origin: Textiles Day is an informal craft observance that gives hobbyists and professionals a reason to show off their fiber-based creations.
holidays.funFact: The oldest known textile fragments are dyed flax fibers found in a Georgian cave, dating back roughly 34,000 years.

holidays.name: Orchid Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the elegant, finicky, and occasionally murder-prone-for-houseplant-owners orchid, one of the largest flowering plant families on Earth.
holidays.origin: Orchid Day is an unofficial flower-appreciation observance, popular with plant lovers and gardening clubs who use the day to swap tips on keeping the divas alive.
holidays.funFact: Vanilla, the world's favorite ice cream flavor, comes from an orchid, making it the only edible fruit of the orchid family that most people eat daily.

holidays.name: Lumpy Rug Day
holidays.description: A day for those who prefer to sweep their problems under the rug, then admit the rug looks a little lumpy. It encourages a laugh about all the messes we hide instead of cleaning.
holidays.origin: A tongue-in-cheek unofficial observance shared among humor-calendar enthusiasts, poking fun at procrastination and half-hearted housekeeping.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'sweep it under the rug' has been used in English since at least the early 1900s to describe hiding embarrassing matters.
